title: Split Filter Controller CSS modules
description: Split eit-frontend.css and editor cadence CSS into base, shared, and type-specific module files while preserving load order.
objective: Make future visual polish land in the right CSS module instead of expanding one large stylesheet.
expected_outputs: CSS module folder for Filter Controller under assets/css/filter-controller/
Base, shared, and type CSS files imported from assets/css/eit-frontend.css
Stable WordPress enqueue order through the existing eit-frontend handle
No bundler introduced; editor cadence CSS remains fail-open and separately bounded
acceptance_criteria: Existing widget output keeps the same visual baseline after extraction.
Each CSS module stays within DEC-EIT-014 line budgets.
verification: CSS brace check passes through the Filter Controller robustness harness with imported stylesheet resolution.
php scripts/verify-line-budget.php --strict passes and no longer reports assets/css/eit-frontend.css.
CSS modules under assets/css/filter-controller/ stay below the DEC-EIT-014 line budget; largest module is range.css at 308 lines.
./scripts/wp.sh eval-file wp-content/plugins/elementor-implementation-toolkit/scripts/verify-filter-controller-robustness.php passes with 49 passed, 0 failed, and 6 Guilherme-owned visual QA skips.
Plugin commit e3970e0 pushed to origin/main.

budgets.validation_budget: CSS check, WP-CLI, line-budget, diff checks

risks: Load-order mistakes can make existing controls appear broken.
Splitting CSS without naming conventions can make future work harder instead of easier.
